rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; number serialization follows ECMAScript JSON.stringify/Number serialization, for which negative zero serializes as 0.
divergence_trap: An implementation that preserves the lexical token may emit {

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; numbers are serialized as ECMAScript IEEE-754 doubles. 2^53 is exactly representable.
divergence_trap: None for a conforming ECMAScript Number serializer; an arbitrary-precision JSON-number implementation may incorrectly preserve a different numeric model.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; parsing into an IEEE-754 binary64 number and subsequent ECMAScript serialization rounds 9007199254740993 to the representable value 9007199254740992.
divergence_trap: Arbitrary-precision JSON parsers that retain the decimal integer exactly may incorrectly emit 9007199254740993 rather than the JCS/ECMAScript Number result.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; ECMAScript uses fixed-point notation in this magnitude range, including 10^20.
divergence_trap: A serializer that always prefers exponent notation may emit {
:1e+20}, which is not the canonical ECMAScript/JCS representation.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; ECMAScript switches to exponential notation at 10^21.
divergence_trap: :1000000000000000000000}; a non-ECMAScript exponent formatter may emit 1E21 instead of the required lowercase e and explicit plus sign.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; ECMAScript uses fixed notation at 10^-6.
divergence_trap: A serializer that always uses scientific notation may emit {
:1e-6}, which is not the canonical JCS representation.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3; ECMAScript switches to exponential notation below 10^-6.
divergence_trap: :0.0000001}; a naive scientific formatter may use 1E-7 rather than the required lowercase e and no unnecessary zero padding.

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.2; only the required JSON escapes are used, and the solidus U+002F need not and does not get escaped. Reverse solidus and quotation mark are escaped; control characters use their short escapes where defined.
divergence_trap: A serializer that habitually escapes / may emit
, producing different bytes. A serializer that uses non-canonical forms for control characters can also diverge.

certainty.rule: RFC 8785 Sections 3.2.2.2 and 3.2.3; JCS performs no Unicode normalization, while strings are serialized from Unicode values. A valid surrogate pair represents the corresponding non-BMP Unicode scalar value.
certainty.divergence_trap: A Unicode-normalizing implementation may incorrectly make the first two string values identical in representation. An implementation that preserves literal surrogate-pair escape spelling instead of serializing the Unicode character can diverge.

certainty.rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.3; object property names are sorted by their UTF-16 code-unit sequences, not by Unicode code-point order. U+10000 is encoded as D800 DC00, so it sorts before U+E000.
certainty.divergence_trap: A naive implementation that sorts decoded Unicode strings by code point can order U+E000 before U+10000 and emit {

certainty.rule: RFC 8785 Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.3; empty arrays/objects serialize as [] and {}, while object member names are recursively sorted using UTF-16 ordering.
certainty.divergence_trap: An implementation that sorts only the outermost object can leave the nested members as {

certainty.rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.1 and the JCS uniqueness requirement: object property names must be unique. Duplicate member names make the input unsuitable for deterministic JCS canonicalization.
certainty.divergence_trap: A parser using last-wins semantics may silently reduce the input to {
:2}; a first-wins parser may reduce it to {
:1}. Both discard the fact that the original JSON had duplicate names.
